summary: The Big Bad Wolf is a fictional wolf from cautionary tales, including several of Grimms' Fairy Tales. It has become a standard figure of a menacing predator. It appears in tales such as "Little Red Riding Hood" and "The Three Little Pigs". 19th-century folklorists read the Red Riding Hood tale as a solar myth, with the wolf as night swallowing the sun. Ethologist Valerius Geist argued the fables warned of a real risk of wolf attacks. Disney's version first appeared in the 1933 short Three Little Pigs, which introduced the song "Who's Afraid of the Big Bad Wolf?". The short's success led to several sequels, in which the Practical Pig always defeats him. From 1936 the character also appeared in Disney comics. There he is named Zeke and has a kind son, Li'l Bad Wolf, who befriends the pigs. He also appears in Disney television series such as House of Mouse.
